rules.summary: Inside a schedule the game only checks three places: JojaMart and Railroad (use '<Loc>_Replacement' if present, else fall back) and CommunityCenter (always fall back while not accessible). The accessibility rules (Railroad DaysPlayed > 31, CC event 191393, JojaMart until any player saw 191393) are right.

Only JojaMart and Railroad entries use '<Location>_Replacement' ('location x y facing'). For CommunityCenter the game ignores any replacement and drops to the fallback schedule. The data has CommunityCenter_Replacement for Clint, Maru and Penny, which the game never uses; JojaMart_Replacement exists for Jodi, Pam and Sam; no NPC has Railroad_Replacement.

On a blocked entry with no usable replacement, parsing restarts with 'default' if the NPC has it, else 'spring'. Edge case: the fallback goes through the same check; if it would loop back to a key already visited, the game returns an empty schedule (the NPC stays put). It does not try the next candidate key, which the planner does.
Married Penny tries marriageJob on Tue/Wed/Fri, Maru and Harvey on Tue/Thu; hard-coded by name.
Heart count for schedule keys = max(0, highest friendship points with this NPC across all players) / 250.
First check: if Green Rain and year 1, try 'GreenRain'.

For each active passive festival: married NPCs try marriage_<Id>_<n> then marriage_<Id>; others <Id>_<n> then <Id>; n = dayOfMonth - StartDay + 1. This comes after GreenRain and a Ginger Island resort visit, and before everything else.

Married: marriage_<season>_<day>; then marriageJob on job days; then marriage_<weekday> only if not raining (Game1.isRaining); otherwise no schedule. GreenRain, resort-visit (islandScheduleName) and passive-festival keys come before this.

The order matches: <season>_<day>; <day>_<h> for h=hearts..1; <day>; Pam 'bus' if the current player has ccVault; if raining, 50% rain2 then rain; <season>_<weekday>_<h> for h=hearts,hearts-2,..>0; <season>_<weekday>; <weekday>_<h> same steps; <weekday>; <season>; spring_<weekday>; spring. Keys match case-insensitively.
Pam tries 'bus' when Game1.player has mail ccVault (host's mail is used for the bus itself).
rain2 is tried first only if Game1.random.NextBool() (unseeded, so not predictable); otherwise 'rain'.

TryLoadSchedule(key) returns success as soon as the key exists in the NPC's schedule data, whatever the parse gives. An empty or failed parse leaves the NPC with no or empty schedule; the game does not move on to the next candidate key.

rules.summary: Entries are '/'-separated. Each is: time (an 'a' prefix means arrive by), optional location (if the second token is a number the previous location is kept), x, y, optional facing (default 2), then an optional end behaviour/animation and an optional quoted dialogue key.

'bed' appears as the location of an entry ('<time> bed', 69 uses, mostly marriage_ and festival keys). For an unmarried NPC it means the location and tile of the last entry of their 'default' (else 'spring') schedule, falling back to their home; for a spouse it's the Bus Stop at (9,23) facing left, from where they head home. It also plays '<name>_sleep' if that animation exists.

'GOTO <key>' as the first command (or after a MAIL/NOT condition) swaps in that key's schedule. 'GOTO season' means the current season's key (spring if missing). 'GOTO no_schedule' means no schedule. A missing target falls back to 'spring'.

The game evaluates the conditions. 'MAIL <id>': if the host has that mail (or the world-state ID is set) it skips the next command (usually a GOTO) and uses the rest; if not, it uses the next command. 'NOT friendship <NPC> <hearts> ...': if any farmer has at least those hearts with any listed NPC, the day becomes 'spring'; otherwise the rest is used. 'FRIENDSHIP' is not a schedule keyword.
Times past midnight are 2400+hhmm style: 2530 is 1:30 AM and 2600 is 2:00 AM (Utility.ConvertTimeToMinutes treats them as minutes after midnight). Schedules use values like 2530.

Schedules load from Characters/schedules/<Name> (keys matched case-insensitively). Exception: Leo uses Characters/schedules/LeoMainland whenever his DefaultMap isn't IslandHut. 'template' isn't an NPC.

The game's order is: (1) Stardrop Tea is a special taste; (2) universal category match (love, hate, like, dislike); (3) universal context-tag match overrides; (4) universal item-ID match (love, hate, like, dislike, neutral) overrides; (5) any Type 'Arch' item becomes dislike (like for Penny and Dwarf); (6) if still neutral and not on Universal_Neutral by ID: edibility < 0 (and not -300) means hate, otherwise sell price < 20 means dislike; (7) personal item IDs in order love, hate, like, dislike, neutral; (8) personal context tags in that order; (9) personal categories in that order, only if no universal item-ID matched and the category isn't 0.

rules.summary: Universal category check order is love, hate, like, dislike, and Universal_Neutral is not checked by category. Note: Universal_Hate's '0' token also matches every category-0 object, so uncategorised objects are hated unless an ID/tag rule overrides.
Universal item-ID order is love, hate, like, dislike, neutral. A neutral ID match also blocks the price/edibility override. Universal context tags are checked between the category and ID steps.

The game applies these overrides and the data to do it is in Data/Objects. Artifacts (Type Arch) become dislike (Penny and Dwarf: like). A still-neutral item, unless listed by ID in Universal_Neutral, becomes hate if edibility < 0 and != -300, else dislike if Price < 20 (e.g. Stone, Fiber).

Bundle ctor: the bundle is complete when the number of completed ingredients is at least numberOfIngredientSlots (field [4], else the ingredient count). When an item bundle completes, every flag in its save array is set true. Vault bundles set only flag [0].
Depositing consumes the stack (ConsumeStack) and marks one ingredient slot done, so a physical item can fill only one slot.

This reservation policy fits the game. Since 1.6 HandlePartialDonation lets you top up one slot from several qualifying stacks (mixed qualities, all at least the required one) in one sitting, but ReturnPartialDonations hands an unfinished slot back when the bundle check runs or the menu closes. So a slot can only be finished when enough qualifying items are in hand together. Note: donating uses only the player inventory; chest stock must be carried first.
Vault bundles are completed with gold through the purchase button (whichArea 4); deposits are not used.

Bundles match by exact qualified item id (unqualified ids are objects), by category for negative ids (a Dinosaur Egg also counts for -5 eggs), and need at least the asked quality. Names are never used, so shared display names (Egg 176/180, Large Egg 174/182) can't be confused.

Notes appear: Crafts Room always, Pantry and Fish Tank after 1 complete bundle, Boiler Room after 2, Bulletin Board after 3, Vault after 4, the Joja 'Missing' bundle after the CC ceremony (event 191393); never once each bundle's ingredient flags in the room are all set. A bundle counts as complete only when every entry of its save list (3 per ingredient) is true, so paid Vault bundles (only entry 0 set) don't count.
A finished area never gets its note back (shouldNoteAppearInArea returns false once every bundle there is done), so treating it as not locked is fine.

Field crops are HoeDirt terrain features (written as TerrainFeature xsi:type="HoeDirt") with a non-nil crop. Garden pots are Objects of xsi:type IndoorPot whose dirt lives in a child element named hoeDirt; because that field's declared type is already HoeDirt, the serializer writes no xsi:type on it, so a search for xsi:type=HoeDirt misses every crop in a garden pot.

phaseDays is the list of days per growth phase (already shortened by Speed-Gro/Agriculturist/paddy bonus at planting) with a final 99999 marker. Each growing night dayOfCurrentPhase goes up by one (capped at the phase length); when it reaches the phase length the crop moves to the next phase at day 0, skipping zero-length phases. The crop is ready once currentPhase is the last index. So days left = (phase length - dayOfCurrentPhase) + the later real phases, exactly as the planner computes; each of those days needs the tile watered.

After a regrowing crop is harvested the game sets fullGrown=true and dayOfCurrentPhase=RegrowDays; each watered night it decrements, and the crop is harvestable again when it is <= 0 (it stays in the last phase). So days left = max(0, dayOfCurrentPhase).

indexOfHarvest is serialized as the unqualified item id of Data/Crops HarvestItemId (e.g. 256); stripping a (O) prefix is harmless. Caveats: wild-seed crops store their real (random/seasonal) produce in overrideHarvestItemId; Sunflower's id is switched to 431 (seeds) during harvest only for the bonus drop.

Location terrainFeatures is a dictionary keyed by Vector2 tile; the HoeDirt is the value. Garden-pot dirt has no key of its own (it is inside the pot object, whose objects-dictionary key is the tile).

HoeDirt.state: 0 dry, 1 watered, 2 invisible (unused dirt). In a fresh save state 1 means the tile is already watered for that day (rain, sprinkler, retaining soil or a paddy near water set it during the overnight update).
crop/dead=true marks a dead crop; readyForHarvest is false for it and harvest gives nothing.

1.6 saves have no regrowAfterHarvest element any more (the field was removed; regrowth comes from Data/Crops RegrowDays via Crop.RegrowsAfterHarvest). fullGrown only becomes true after the first harvest of a regrowing crop. So a regrowing crop that hasn't been picked yet (fullGrown=false) is reported as non-regrowing by the planner. Confirmed: no regrowAfterHarvest in the local 1.6.15 saves.
HoeDirt/fertilizer holds the fertilizer item id; 1.6 writes it qualified, e.g. (O)368 (seen in all local 1.6 saves), older saves may be unqualified. Only one fertilizer can be on a tile at a time.
Growth days completed = sum of earlier phases + dayOfCurrentPhase while the crop is still growing; once in the final phase the first-growth count is no longer meaningful.

A planted crop ripens after days_left more watered nights, so with daily watering it is ready on today + days_left.

Every night, an outdoor crop whose data Seasons does not include the location's current season is killed (the date and season advance before locations update). So an outdoor crop must be in season on every day from planting to harvest. Greenhouse and all Ginger Island locations ignore seasons; crops in indoor locations (pots) never check.

Planted on day d and watered every day, a crop ripens the morning of d + sum(phases); latest plant day = last harvest day - grow. grow here must be the trimmed phases if Speed-Gro/Agriculturist/paddy bonus apply.

At harvest the game computes g = 0.2*(FarmingLevel/10) + 0.2*F*((FarmingLevel+2)/12) + 0.01, where F is the tile's fertilizer quality level (0 none, 1 Basic, 2 Quality, 3 Deluxe) and FarmingLevel is the effective level including food buffs. It then draws independent rolls from one tile/day-seeded RNG: only when F >= 3, an iridium roll succeeds with chance g/2; otherwise a gold roll with chance g; otherwise silver with chance min(0.75, 2g), and with F >= 3 a failed gold roll is always at least silver. The result is clamped to the crop's HarvestMinQuality/HarvestMaxQuality (Fiber and Qi Fruit are capped at normal). The planner's formula is exactly g. For no fertilizer, Basic or Quality (F<3) iridium is impossible, so g = P(gold) = P(gold or better).

At harvest the game computes g = 0.2*(FarmingLevel/10) + 0.2*F*((FarmingLevel+2)/12) + 0.01, where F is the tile's fertilizer quality level (0 none, 1 Basic, 2 Quality, 3 Deluxe) and FarmingLevel is the effective level including food buffs. It then draws independent rolls from one tile/day-seeded RNG: only when F >= 3, an iridium roll succeeds with chance g/2; otherwise a gold roll with chance g; otherwise silver with chance min(0.75, 2g), and with F >= 3 a failed gold roll is always at least silver. The result is clamped to the crop's HarvestMinQuality/HarvestMaxQuality (Fiber and Qi Fruit are capped at normal). With Deluxe Fertilizer (F=3): P(iridium)=g/2, P(gold)=(1-g/2)*g, P(silver)=the rest, P(normal)=0. So P(gold or better) = g/2 + (1-g/2)*g = 1.5g - g^2/2, larger than g. Plugging F=3 into the gold formula alone understates gold-or-better.

Quality boost level: (O)368 Basic = 1, (O)369 Quality = 2, (O)919 Deluxe = 3, anything else 0 (Speed-Gro and retaining soils add no quality). These numbers are hard-coded in the game, not in any Data asset, so they cannot be derived at runtime.

Quality is rolled inside harvest, using the Farming level (with buffs) and tile fertilizer at that moment, from an RNG seeded by tile x/y, days played and the game id. So ripe-but-unpicked crops still roll; the outcome for a given tile on a given day is fixed.

On the first night of a new season an outdoor crop whose Seasons lacks the new season is marked dead (in winter it is then removed outright). A crop with days_left <= days remaining in the season can still be harvested by day 28. Exempt: greenhouse, Ginger Island, indoor pots.

Planner policy (which fertilizer to plan with), not a game rule. The mechanics it relies on are verified: Basic = level 1 in the quality formula, and it must go on before the crop sprouts (currentPhase 0).
Skill levels top out at 10 (checkForLevelGain looks at levels 1-10). The value used in quality and stack formulas is FarmingLevel, which adds food buffs and can exceed 10.

Outdoors a crop survives each night whose new season is in its Seasons list, so it runs through a consecutive block of listed seasons and dies the night after day 28 of the last one. Crops listing all four seasons (Fiber Seeds, Qi Bean, Cactus) never die of season and carry from Winter into Spring; the planner's run stops at Winter 28.

Shop stock is gated by each Data/Shops item Condition (SEASON x, YEAR n meaning year >= n, DAYS_PLAYED, etc.); Sandy's Oasis needs the bus. The planner's three gates are right as far as they go. Not modelled: Pierre's Missing Stock List lets Pierre sell out-of-season seeds at 1.5x; JojaMart stocks most seeds (x1.25 for non-members); the Traveling Cart's random stock; shop closing days; the profit-margin setting scales seed prices.

First harvest after grow days, then (harvested on the day it ripens) every RegrowDays, until the crop dies; single-harvest crops replanted the same day give floor(days/grow) harvests. Matches the game's countdown.
Ripe on the morning of d + grow; a crop that ripens on day 28 can be picked that day, and the out-of-season kill only runs overnight. So d + grow <= last day is right.

Harvest count = uniform integer in [HarvestMinStack, max(Min, Max) + floor(FarmingLevel * HarvestMaxIncreasePerFarmingLevel)], then one more for each success of repeated rolls at min(0.9, ExtraHarvestChance), then (hand/Junimo grab harvests only) doubled with a tiny luck chance (~0.0001 + luck terms). The bonus to the max is truncated to an integer. Only Unmilled Rice has a per-level increase (0.1), so its max goes from 1 to 2 only at Farming 10.

IsPaddyCrop is true for Rice Shoot (273) and Taro Tuber (831) only. Excluding them is planner policy. Game behaviour if modelled: within 3 tiles (7x7 box) of water a paddy crop is watered automatically every night and gets +0.25 growth speed; elsewhere it needs normal watering.

No shop stocks Ancient Seeds (499): it is in no Data/Shops entry and is ExcludeFromRandomSale, so the Traveling Cart can't roll it. But they can be made: a Seed Maker turns Ancient Fruit into Ancient Seeds, and the museum gives them (donating the Ancient Seed artifact 114 rewards 1 Ancient Seeds plus the recipe to craft more from that artifact). Ancient Fruit regrows every 7 days, so 'one harvest' never applies to it. Planted outdoors in Spring it first fruits after 28 days and keeps fruiting until Fall 28. Data/Crops also forbids Ancient Seeds in garden pots.
rules.fix: Treat Ancient Seeds as replantable once the player has a Seed Maker (an Ancient Fruit makes more seeds); note pots are not allowed.

A crop is protected if the straight-line (Euclidean) tile distance to any scarecrow is strictly less than its radius: 9 by default, 17 for names starting with 'Deluxe', or a crow_scare_radius_N context tag. Anything whose name contains 'arecrow' or has the crow_scare tag counts, so Rarecrows protect with radius 9.

Each night on the Farm only: attempts = min(4, cropsOnFarm // 16) where cropsOnFarm counts every HoeDirt with any crop (seedlings, ripe, dead). Each attempt has a 30% chance, then up to 10 random terrain-feature picks to find a crop past phase 1; an unprotected one is destroyed. So 16+ crops is the threshold.
Crops with IsRaised (Green Bean, Hops, Grape in vanilla) block movement for everything except Junimo harvesters.
Crafting needs the recipe in the player's craftingRecipes; Sprinkler/Quality/Iridium come at Farming 2/6/9 and Scarecrow at Farming 1.

Pure geometry: centres on (x + 2y) mod 5 = 0 give each tile exactly one of centre/N/S/E/W cover, so basic-sprinkler pluses tile the plane with no gaps or overlaps. Each sprinkler occupies its centre tile (not watered), so 4 of every 5 tiles hold crops.

The season kill only applies when the location is outdoors and doesn't ignore seasons. Greenhouse (isGreenhouse) and every IslandLocation ignore seasons. Also exempt: any crop in a non-outdoor location, i.e. garden pots in the farmhouse, cabins, sheds, etc.
rules.fix: Treat any indoor location as no-wilt (location isOutdoors=false), not just names starting Greenhouse/Island; and pot crops outdoors do wilt.

rules.summary: With daily watering a crop needing days_left more nights ripens on today + days_left; if that is after day 28 and the next season isn't listed, it is killed the first night of the new season. Exactly days_left > 28 - today.
The date (and season) advance before crops update, so the night after day 28 kills out-of-season outdoor crops; in Winter they are also removed from the tile.

Missed watering never kills a crop: an unwatered crop just doesn't advance that night. A crop is only marked dead by (1) the season kill for outdoor crops out of season, or (2) a lightning strike (storm days) on the tile when no lightning rod takes it. Crows, giant crops and tools remove crops rather than leaving dead ones.
rules.fix: Explain dead crops as 'season change or lightning', never 'missed watering'.

rules.summary: Without speed boosts, a crop planted today is ready sum(DaysInPhase) watered nights later.

Day 28 is the last harvest day of a crop's last consecutive listed season; multi-season crops carry on. Crops listing all four seasons (Fiber, Qi Fruit, Cactus) never stop outdoors, so Winter 28 is not their end.
rules.fix: Let crops whose Seasons contains all four seasons run past Winter 28.

rules.summary: Speed boost: (O)465 Speed-Gro 0.10, (O)466 Deluxe Speed-Gro 0.25, (O)918 Hyper Speed-Gro 0.33 (as 32-bit floats). Hard-coded in the game, not in any Data asset, so not derivable.

Profession 5 (Agriculturist) adds 0.1, additive with fertilizer; a paddy crop near water adds another 0.25 (not modelled by the planner). Applied only when the crop is planted or fertilized, using that farmer's professions; existing crops don't speed up later.

The game resets the phases, sums them, takes ceil(total * boost) (single-precision product) days off one per phase per pass, at most 3 passes, never reducing the first phase below 1, skipping zero-length phases and the final 99999. The planner's loop matches. Float32 vs float64 makes no difference for any non-paddy boost with totals 1-39; with the paddy +0.25 it differs at total 25 (0.25+0.25+0.1 and 0.33+0.25+0.1 cases).

Growth only happens on nights the tile was watered (or for crops with NeedsWatering=false, e.g. Fiber, always). So no growth overnight usually means it was dry. False positives: applying Speed-Gro between the two saves resets/shrinks phaseDays so the computed growth can drop; replanting the same crop on the same tile; and crops that never need water can't be 'missed'.
rules.fix: Skip crops with NeedsWatering=false, and only flag when phaseDays is unchanged between the two saves.

rules.summary: Harvests left = 1 + (end - today - grow) // regrow for a regrower, matching the regrow countdown; income multiplies by expected stack and base price (quality not included).

Rain, Storm and Green Rain all set IsRaining; in the morning every HoeDirt (state != 2) in outdoor locations where it is raining is set watered, and outdoor garden pots too. Weather is per location context (Ginger Island has its own; the Desert never rains).
Crops 499 (Ancient Seeds) -> 454 Ancient Fruit, Spring/Summer/Fall, phases 2,7,7,7,5 = 28 days, RegrowDays 7.
Winter isn't in its Seasons, so outdoors it is killed the night into Winter 1 (and removed); Fall 28 is the last outdoor harvest.

The Greenhouse is not outdoors and ignores seasons, so crops never die there and any crop with at least one season can be planted any time; its fertilizer isn't cleared at season change and empty dirt there never decays.

Fertilizer belongs to the dirt, not the plant: a tile holds one fertilizer at a time and the game refuses a second (same or different). It stays after a single-harvest crop is picked, so a replant on the same tile reuses it. It is lost when: the season changes and the tile has no live in-season crop (greenhouse/island excepted); or empty dirt decays (10% a night on the Farm, 80% on day 1 of a month; never in the greenhouse).
rules.fix: Say 'one fertilizer per tile at a time; it stays for replants in the same season' rather than 'for the plant's life'.

rules.summary: Only Basic (368) and Quality (369) Fertilizer are refused once currentPhase != 0 (sprouted). Deluxe Fertilizer (919), all Speed-Gros and all retaining soils can be added to a growing crop (if the tile has no fertilizer yet). Applying a Speed-Gro mid-growth re-trims the phases.
rules.fix: Deluxe Fertilizer and Speed-Gro can go on after sprouting; only Basic/Quality cannot.

rules.summary: The quality level is read from the tile at every harvest, so it applies to each regrow harvest; speed boosts only trim the initial phaseDays, and RegrowDays is untouched, so they help the first harvest only (same for Agriculturist).
Basic Fertilizer: 2 Sap -> 1, learned at Farming 1. Pierre also sells it from day 15 of Year 1 (DAYS_PLAYED 15) at item Price 50 x DefaultMarkup 2 = 100g.

Mean of the uniform draw is (Min + max(Min,Max))/2 (the game only draws when either is > 1, same mean), plus a geometric run of extra rolls with mean p/(1-p), p = min(0.9, ExtraHarvestChance). Not included (intentionally, it is a separate field): the per-level max increase; also the luck double (negligible, < 0.1%).

Harvest count = uniform integer in [HarvestMinStack, max(Min, Max) + floor(FarmingLevel * HarvestMaxIncreasePerFarmingLevel)], then one more for each success of repeated rolls at min(0.9, ExtraHarvestChance), then (hand/Junimo grab harvests only) doubled with a tiny luck chance (~0.0001 + luck terms). The bonus to the max is truncated to an integer. Only Unmilled Rice has a per-level increase (0.1), so its max goes from 1 to 2 only at Farming 10.
RegrowsAfterHarvest is RegrowDays > 0; harvest stops (crop removed) when RegrowDays <= 0. Vanilla uses -1 for none.
IsRaised sets raisedSeeds, which makes the dirt impassable (except to Junimos).
IsPaddyCrop drives isPaddyCrop (auto-watering near water and +0.25 speed).

Keg: fruit (category_fruits) -> Wine at 3x price in 10000 min; vegetables (category_vegetable) -> Juice at floor(2.25x) in 6000 min. Jar: fruit -> Jelly, vegetable -> Pickles, both 2x+50 in 4000 min. But the Keg checks specific items first: Wheat -> Beer, Hops -> Pale Ale (both vegetables), Coffee Bean -> Coffee, Tea Leaves -> Green Tea, Honey -> Mead, Rice -> Vinegar; edible forage greens also make Juice/Pickles. Flowers make nothing in these machines (only flavour Honey via a Bee House).

rules.summary: Profession id 1 is Tiller (Farmer.tiller = 1) and gives x1.1. earn.py applies it to every crop it ranks. Coffee Bean, Sweet Gem Berry, Fiber and wild-seed forage would wrongly get it if they were ever ranked.
Profession id 4 is Artisan, x1.4 on category -26. Wine, Juice, Jelly and Pickles are all -26.
This per-day uplift is a planner metric. The artisan prices it uses are right (the product's quality is always normal whatever the input quality, and Artisan applies only to the product).
rules.fix: Its inputs need two fixes. (1) The 'days' value comes from minutes/1440, but a machine ages 1,600 minutes per 6am-to-6am day, so wine is 6.25 days, juice 3.75 and jelly/pickles 2.5. (2) For a Tiller, the raw price should include x1.1; the artisan product never gets Tiller. Also, Wheat, Hops and Tea Leaves are vegetables that a Keg turns into Beer, Pale Ale and Green Tea, not juice.

A machine's rules are tried in order and specific ones come first: in a Keg, Wheat makes Beer, Hops Pale Ale, Tea Leaves Green Tea (180 minutes), Honey Mead, 5 Coffee Beans Coffee, Rice Vinegar; then vegetables (and edible greens that aren't mushrooms) make Juice and fruit makes Wine. rules.summary: The output is picked uniformly from a candidate list. Each mature tree within the 7x7 area adds one candidate by type: oak gives Morel, maple Red (90%) or Purple (10%), pine Chanterelle, mystic tree Purple, any other tree the generic roll. The generic roll is Purple 5%, else Red 15%, else Common. On top of that come max(1, floor(0.75 x all trees counted)) generic candidates. The fixed 40/5/50% figures are approximations that depend on the tree mix.
rules.fix: Compute the odds from the tree mix. With only maples, for example, maple candidates are 90% Red / 10% Purple, diluted by about 3/7 generic candidates.

SaveGameInfo seasonForSaveGame is a nullable int written from Game1.seasonIndex at the start of each new day (0 spring, 1 summer, 2 fall, 3 winter); the main save's root currentSeason is the lowercase season name.
Object quality constants are 0 normal, 1 silver, 2 gold, 4 iridium; 3 is never assigned.

1.6 FruitTree stores treeId = the sapling's object id, which is the key of Data/FruitTrees; each entry's Fruit list gives the fruit (628 Cherry 638, 629 Apricot 634, 630 Orange 635, 631 Peach 636, 632 Pomegranate 637, 633 Apple 613, 69 Banana 91, 835 Mango 834).

Pre-1.6 saves carry treeType (0-8) and indexOfFruit; the fruit ids listed match the fruit each tree produces (613 Apple, 634 Apricot, 635 Orange, 636 Peach, 637 Pomegranate, 638 Cherry, 91 Banana, 834 Mango). The 1.6 migrator maps treeType 0,1,2,3,4,5,7,8 to saplings 628,629,630,631,632,633,69,835.

FruitTree.daysUntilMature defaults to 28 and drops by growthRate each day (only when the tree isn't blocked); growth stage is derived from it and the tree is fully grown (stage 4) once it is <= 0. It keeps going negative afterwards (used for fruit quality by age). Fruit still only appears in the tree's Seasons (or in the greenhouse/island).

CommunityCenter.areasComplete is a 6-element bool array indexed 0 Pantry, 1 Crafts Room, 2 Fish Tank, 3 Boiler Room, 4 Vault, 5 Bulletin Board (area ids 6-8, Abandoned Joja Mart etc., are not in the array). An entry is set during the room-restore cutscene.

The CommunityCenter location serializes <bundles> (backed by the world state): key = bundle index (the number after the slash in the bundleData key), value = bool array whose length is the number of space-separated tokens in the ingredient field, i.e. 3 x ingredient count. The real save has 31 entries; the >=20 heuristic finds it, though matching the CommunityCenter GameLocation directly is more robust.

SaveGame.bundleData holds this farm's bundle definitions keyed 'Room/index' in Data/Bundles format (name/reward/ingredients/colour/slots/sprite/display name). It has been in saves since remixed bundles arrived (1.5); a save without it uses Data/Bundles.

Inventory and chest items are <Item xsi:type=...>. Plain objects are xsi:type 'Object' with unqualified itemId, parentSheetIndex, price and category. But 1.6 also writes Object subclasses: every preserve/artisan good with a source item (Wine, Jelly, Pickles, Juice, Dried fruit, flavoured Honey, Roe...) and coloured flowers (Poppy, Summer Spangle...) are xsi:type 'ColoredObject'. The real save holds Poppy and Summer Spangle as ColoredObject.

Object.price is the object's own base price. For flavoured goods it is set from the source item when the good is created (e.g. a Pickled Tomato in the save has price 170, not the base Pickles price), and sellToStorePrice starts from it.
Item.stack serializes as <stack> and quality as <quality>; a stack is always >= 1 for a real item.
Object.bigCraftable is serialized; when true the itemId is a big-craftable id (qualified '(BC)'), not an object id, so the object id/price/category must not be used.

Objects 174 and 182 are both named 'Large Egg' (same price 95, edibility 15, category -5); 182 is the brown one. Bundle ingredients match by qualified id. The Animal bundle lists 186, 182, 174, 438, 440, 442 but needs only 4 of the 6.
data: Data/Bundles 'Pantry/4' ingredient list and slot count (field 4)

rules.summary: Pockets are the first <player>/<items>; placed chests and mini-fridges are <Object xsi:type='Chest'> with <items>. Not covered: the farmhouse and island-farmhouse fridge (serialized as a <fridge> element under the FarmHouse/IslandFarmHouse location, no xsi:type), Junimo chests (their contents live in root <globalInventories>, not on the chest), auto-grabbers (contents in <heldObject xsi:type='Chest'>), and farmhands' inventories. Chests in sheds/barns sit inside a building's <indoors> element, so the nearest GameLocation ancestor is the Farm.

Root SaveGame carries currentSeason (lowercase name), dayOfMonth and year; in 1.6 saves these tags occur only at root, and <money> occurs under <player> first. First-in-document-order works but reading root children directly is safer.
player/<money> is the Farmer._money property: the shared team wallet, or the host's own wallet when separate wallets are on.
Data/Tools names the axe tiers Axe (UpgradeLevel 0), Copper Axe 1, Steel Axe 2, Gold Axe 3, Iridium Axe 4.
Axe items are <Item xsi:type='Axe'> with <upgradeLevel> equal to the Data/Tools UpgradeLevel (0-4).

When you buy an upgrade at Clint's, the old tool is removed from inventory and toolBeingUpgraded is set to a copy of the NEW tool (e.g. Copper Axe, upgradeLevel 1) with daysLeftForToolUpgrade = 2; it stays there until collected. So owned tier = its upgradeLevel - 1 is correct.

Data/Tools fishing rods: Bamboo Pole UpgradeLevel 0, Training Rod 1, Fiberglass Rod 2, Iridium Rod 3, Advanced Iridium Rod 4. The planner's own ordinal (Training 0 < Bamboo 1) is a ranking, not the game's upgradeLevel.
Farmer serializes farmingLevel, fishingLevel, foragingLevel, miningLevel, combatLevel (and luckLevel); these are unbuffed base levels.

friendshipData is a dictionary keyed by NPC name whose value is a Friendship with Points, GiftsThisWeek, GiftsToday, TalkedToToday, ProposalRejected, Status (Friendly/Dating/Engaged/Married/Divorced), Proposer, RoommateMarriage; hearts = Points / 250.

Farmer.spouse holds the NPC name for both engagement and marriage (also a roommate). The 'engaged' suffix is a pre-1.3 format that SaveMigrator_1_3 strips; since 1.3 engagement is friendshipData[spouse].Status == Engaged.
rules.fix: Detect engagement from friendshipData Status 'Engaged' (and roommate from RoommateMarriage), not a suffix. Read player/spouse rather than the first <spouse> anywhere.

rules.summary: mailReceived is a set of <string> mail/flag ids. Letters that have arrived but not yet been read sit in player/<mailbox>, and flags queued for tomorrow in <mailForTomorrow> (normally empty at save time).
eventsSeen is a string set in 1.6 but still serialized with <int> element names; values can be non-numeric (the real save has 'festival_spring13', 'prizeTicketIntro').

fishCaught: key = qualified fish id '(O)nnn', value = int[2] [times caught, largest size]. Only items whose object type is Fish (or Clam 372) count; trash, fish-pond catches and Algae 167 excluded. The <stats><fishCaught> element is nil in 1.6 and must be skipped (the code does).
cookingRecipes is a dictionary: key = known recipe name (Data/CookingRecipes key), value = times cooked.
craftingRecipes is a dictionary: key = known recipe name (Data/CraftingRecipes key), value = times crafted.
The LibraryMuseum location is named ArchaeologyHouse; museumPieces maps tile (Vector2) -> item id, stored as <string> in 1.6 and <int> in 1.5 saves (confirmed in both).
Root dailyLuck is the team's shared daily luck. The player's effective luck adds +0.025 with the Special Charm and is clamped to [-0.2, 0.2].

Root weatherForTomorrow is the valley (Default context) forecast written after the new day's weather roll: Sun, Rain, Storm, Wind, Snow, GreenRain, Festival or Wedding. Island/Desert have their own in locationWeather. Pre-1.6 saves may hold a legacy int code.

Root isRaining/isLightning/isSnowing/isDebrisWeather are today's valley weather (the save is written after the day's weather is applied). There is no root isGreenRain: green rain is only in locationWeather['Default'] (isGreenRain, and Weather='GreenRain'), and a green-rain day also sets isRaining true.

Storm sets rain+lightning, green rain sets rain, snow excludes rain, so snow > storm > green rain > rain > sun is a consistent order. Wind (isDebrisWeather) is a separate weather the label drops into 'sun'.

Every Building has buildingType. In 1.6 the Farmhouse, Greenhouse (present even before it is repaired), Shipping Bin and Pet Bowl are Buildings too. New construction (daysOfConstructionLeft > 0) already has its final type and finishes on its own; an upgrade in progress (daysUntilUpgrade > 0) keeps the OLD buildingType until it finishes (target in upgradeName).
FarmAnimal.type is the Data/FarmAnimals key (e.g. 'White Chicken', 'Brown Cow'); animals are in each animal building's indoors <animals> dictionary (or the Farm's while outside).

A placed big craftable is an <Object> with bigCraftable true in a location's objects. That includes non-machines (chests, scarecrows, rarecrows, signs, statues, Workbench...) and casks. Sprinkler names all end in 'Sprinkler'. Placed Crab Pots are xsi:type CrabPot with bigCraftable false, so they are in neither list.

Quest base fields serialize as id, completed, dailyQuest, daysLeft, moneyReward, _questTitle/questTitle, _currentObjective. Help Wanted subclasses: ItemDeliveryQuest target/item/number (reward is moneyReward), FishingQuest target/whichFish/numberToFish/numberFished/reward, SlayMonsterQuest monsterName/target/numberToKill/numberKilled/reward, ResourceCollectionQuest target/resource/number/numberCollected/reward. The quest type is the xsi:type (absent for plain story quests).

SpecialOrder serializes questKey, requester, questName and questDescription (tokens like '[Robin_Name]' resolved via Strings/SpecialOrderStrings), orderType ('' town board, 'QiChallenge' Qi), duration, dueDate (absolute WorldDate.TotalDays, 0 = Spring 1 Y1), questState (InProgress/Complete/Failed), preSelectedItems, objectives (xsi:type, currentCount, maxCount, description, acceptableContextTagSets) and rewards. MoneyReward has amount AND multiplier; the payout is amount x multiplier.

Root specialOrders = orders the team has accepted (still listed with questState Complete/Failed until removed); availableSpecialOrders = offers on BOTH boards this week (town and Qi's, told apart by orderType); completedSpecialOrders = keys ever completed.
1.6 keeps days played in the player's stats Values dictionary under key 'daysPlayed' (unsignedInt); older saves had <daysPlayed> under stats (now obsolete_daysPlayed). Spring 1 Y1 = 1.

professions is a set of ints; 1 = Tiller, 4 = Artisan. Tiller multiplies sell price by 1.1 for categories -75 (vegetable), -80 (flower) and -79 (fruit) unless the fruit is a spawned forage object; Artisan multiplies -26 artisan goods by 1.4. Multipliers stack per active farmer's professions (shared wallet).
rules.fix: Apply Tiller to -75/-80 and non-forage -79 only (not forage -81 or forage fruit); note other price professions (Rancher 0, Fisher 6/Angler 8, Tapper 15, Blacksmith 20, Gemologist 23) if the planner prices those goods.

rules.summary: houseUpgradeLevel 1 adds the kitchen (FarmHouse1 map has the 'kitchen' tile action). It only increments when Robin finishes (3 days after paying 10,000g + 450 Wood). The Ginger Island farmhouse also has a kitchen.
rules.fix: Cooking is also possible in the Island farmhouse once it is unlocked; houseUpgradeLevel >= 1 is sufficient but not necessary.

rules.summary: deepestMineLevel is the max mine level entered (excluding the Quarry Mine 77377); Skull Cavern floor N is stored as 120 + N, so values above 120 are Skull Cavern floors.
totalMoneyEarned is farm-wide (team) lifetime earnings; it rises whenever a player's money increases (shipping, sales, quest rewards...), never decreases.
In 1.6 the rusty key is the mail flag 'HasRustyKey' on the host (MasterPlayer.mailReceived). The <hasRustyKey> element is obsolete (nil in 1.6 saves; migrated into mail).
On each save the current files are renamed to <name>_old and SaveGameInfo_old, then the new temp files take their place, so exactly one backup generation exists.
Saves are under Environment ApplicationData/StardewValley/Saves: %APPDATA% on Windows; on Linux and macOS .NET resolves ApplicationData to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, else ~/.config.
rules.fix: Honour $XDG_CONFIG_HOME before ~/.config on Linux/macOS.

rules.summary: Folder name = filtered farmer name + '_' + uniqueIDForThisGame; it holds the main file with the same name, SaveGameInfo, and their _old copies (temporary _STARDEWVALLEYSAVETMP files during a save).
SaveGameInfo is the serialized Game1.player, so its root element is <Farmer>; it has name, farmName, seasonForSaveGame (int), dayOfMonthForSaveGame, yearForSaveGame (plus money, gameVersion etc.).

Each bundle's save list is 3 entries per ingredient; entry i (0-based, in ingredient order) is true once ingredient i was given. A bundle shows as done when that many entries meet its slot count; completing it by donation sets every entry true, buying a Vault bundle sets only entry 0. Decide 'done' first; a done bundle's other entries say nothing about what was given.

landslideDone and canReadJunimoText are mail flags, but beachBridgeFixed is NOT: fixing the beach bridge adds a world-state id, saved in root <worldStateIDs> (and Beach <bridgeFixed>true). Also landslideDone is a real letter: it sits in <mailbox> until read, while the landslide itself is gone from DaysPlayed >= 5.
data: real 1.6.15 save (McClarkies) + 1.5.6 save (Morphic) (1.5.6 save has worldStateIDs beachBridgeFixed, mailReceived does not)
rules.fix: Check beachBridgeFixed in root worldStateIDs (or Beach bridgeFixed). For letter flags check mailReceived OR mailbox; for the mines use daysPlayed >= 5.

rules.summary: Axe upgradeLevel 1 = Copper, 2 = Steel (Data/Tools).

With the planner's own ordinal, Bamboo = 1 and Fiberglass = 2 (Fiberglass also matches the game's upgradeLevel 2). The Training Rod (game upgradeLevel 1) is a working rod but ranks 0 in the planner, so 'tier >= 1 has a rod' excludes it.
rules.fix: Use has_rod (any FishingRod) for 'has a rod'; reserve tier checks for Fiberglass/Iridium.

rules.summary: houseUpgradeLevel 1 = first upgrade, which adds the kitchen.

areasComplete is only set by the CC restore cutscene. On the Joja route areasComplete stays false; buying each Joja development instead queues mail 'cc<Room>' (ccPantry, ccCraftsRoom, ccFishTank, ccBoilerRoom, ccVault) plus 'joja<Room>'. The CC route also gets the same cc<Room> mail.
Planner policy. Game fact behind it: a tree is mature (can fruit in season) when daysUntilMature <= 0; it was planted if a FruitTree with that treeId exists.

Recipe names match Data/CraftingRecipes keys ('Furnace', 'Tapper', 'Mushroom Log', 'Crab Pot') and placed big craftables carry those names. But a placed Crab Pot is an <Object xsi:type='CrabPot'> (bigCraftable false) in a location, so it is neither a 'machine' nor an inventory/chest 'item' in the planner.
data: Data/CraftingRecipes (Tapper 's Foraging 4', Mushroom Log 's Foraging 4', Crab Pot 's Fishing 3', Furnace 'l 2')

rules.summary: Root year is the current year (1-based).

Object category constants: -75 vegetable, -79 fruit, -80 flower, -81 forage ('greens'), -4 fish, -5 egg, -6 milk, -18 sellAtPierresAndMarnies (wool, duck feather, rabbit's foot), -26 artisan, -27 syrup (tapper products), -2 gem, -12 mineral, -14 meat (no vanilla items), -20 junk/trash, -23 sellAtFishShop. -23 is NOT shellfish: it holds Nautilus Shell, Coral, Rainbow Shell, Sea Urchin, Roe, Squid Ink; clams, cockles, mussels, oysters, crabs, lobsters etc. are -4 Fish. -17 (sellAtPierres: Truffle, Sweet Gem Berry) and -28 (monster loot) are missing from the map.
rules.fix: Relabel -23 (beach forage / roe / squid ink); add -17 (Truffle, Sweet Gem Berry) and -28 if they should be sold; derive labels from the game's category display names.

rules.summary: -15 is metalResources (bars, ores, coal, refined quartz, cinder shard, bone fragment...) and -16 buildingResources (wood, stone, clay, fiber, hardwood, battery pack, moss).
Same scale: 0 normal, 1 silver, 2 gold, 4 iridium.
Category-0 objects with Type 'Fish' are exactly Seaweed, Green Algae, White Algae and the Sea/River/Cave Jellies; all 42 Type 'Arch' objects are category 0.

An object can be donated if it is an (O) item without the context tag not_museum_donatable and has tag museum_donatable or type Arch or Minerals. Vanilla uses neither tag, so it is exactly Type Arch (42) + Minerals (53) = 95.
The game's own test is context tag 'crow_scare' OR the name contains 'arecrow' (Scarecrow, Deluxe Scarecrow, Rarecrows). Radius: tag crow_scare_radius_N, else 17 for names starting 'Deluxe', else 9.

Skipping is right but the reason is wrong: crops with no indexOfHarvest are forage crops (forageCrop true; whichForageCrop 1 = Spring Onion patches in the Forest, 2 = Ginger on the island), which the real save shows on the island. No save has indexOfHarvest -1.
<save>_old is the previous save (normally last night's, i.e. daysPlayed one less); checking days_played == today-1 is the right validity test.
1.6 HoeDirt.fertilizer is a qualified item id such as '(O)368' / '(O)370' (seen in the real save).
Exactly these six have IndoorMapType StardewValley.AnimalHouse and ValidOccupantTypes Coop or Barn (MaxOccupants 4/8/12).
Each GameLocation serializes piecesOfHay; only buildable locations with silos hold any (the Farm in vanilla). Capacity is 240 per Silo.
-74 is SeedsCategory (display 'Seed'). It also covers saplings and non-crop seeds; which seeds are crops is the set of Data/Crops keys.
-7 is CookingCategory (display 'Cooking'; -25 ingredients shares the same display name).

Story-quest letters (e.g. spring_19_1) arrive in <mailbox>; the quest is added to the log only when the letter is read (the %item quest% command), which also moves the id into mailReceived. A finished quest leaves the log, but so does a cancelled or expired one.
rules.fix: mailReceived + not in log means 'given and gone' (usually done), not certainly done; mail in <mailbox> means 'arrived, unread, quest not yet given'.

rules.summary: Yes: availableSpecialOrders (both boards) and specialOrders (accepted) are full SpecialOrder objects with objectives, counts and an absolute dueDate (WorldDate.TotalDays). Names/descriptions are tokens to resolve via Strings/SpecialOrderStrings.

Qualified ids are '(O)' + object id for objects; other types use (BC), (T), (W), (F), (H), (B), (S), (P), (TR), (M) etc. The save's Item itemId is unqualified, while quest/order/fishCaught/fertilizer fields are qualified.
museumPieces lists every item currently placed in the museum (donations are permanent), keyed by tile.
The landslide is removed in Mountain.DayUpdate once DaysPlayed >= 5 (Spring 5 Y1), and the 'landslideDone' letter is sent the same morning. It is a real letter, so it sits in <mailbox> until read.
rules.fix: Use daysPlayed >= 5 (or landslideDone in mailReceived OR mailbox).

rules.summary: 'ccDoorUnlock' is added (no letter) by the Town event where Lewis opens the Community Center; 'seenJunimoNote' is added the first time a bundle note is opened (implies the door is open).
'canReadJunimoText' is added directly to mailReceived during the Wizard's forest-vision event (event 112, also if skipped).
'wizardJunimoNote' is queued for tomorrow the first time you open a bundle note (the golden scroll) in the CC; it is a letter, so it is in <mailbox> until read.

The backpack upgrade is not gated by mail: Pierre's counter always offers 24 slots for 2,000g when maxItems is 12, and 36 slots for 10,000g after. 'pierreBackpack' is only an advertisement letter queued the day after your inventory first fills (BackpackTip).
'guildQuest' (Marlon's letter) is queued for tomorrow when mine floor 5 is first generated; being a letter, it is in <mailbox> until read.

Only 'ccPantry' is real mail (no-letter flag delivered next morning, by the CC Pantry or the Joja purchase). 'pantryUnlocked' does not exist in the game; 'greenhouseUnlocked' is a Farm field (<greenhouseUnlocked> on the Farm location), set from ccPantry when the Farm next resets, not a mail id.
rules.fix: Use mail ccPantry or Farm <greenhouseUnlocked>true; drop pantryUnlocked.

rules.summary: 'ccVault' is the real flag, queued (no letter) both when the CC Vault is completed and when the Joja bus development is bought. 'busFixed' and 'paidJoja' appear nowhere in the game code or data.
rules.fix: Keep ccVault only.

rules.summary: Cooking needs a 'kitchen' tile action, which exists in the upgraded farmhouse/cabin (houseUpgradeLevel >= 1) and in the Ginger Island farmhouse.
rules.fix: Also allow cooking when the Island farmhouse is unlocked.

rules.summary: Watching the Queen of Sauce adds the episode's recipe to cookingRecipes immediately if not already known, so the next save has it.

The cooking channel airs only on Sundays (new episode: week = (daysPlayed % 224) / 7, with 224 -> 32) and Wednesdays from daysPlayed > 7 (a rerun picked at random from aired episodes some player hasn't learned). Neither can be watched on another day.
Episodes are Data/TV/CookingChannel (32 entries keyed '1'..'32', value 'Recipe Name/script'); the board text tokens resolve from Strings/SpecialOrderStrings.

Episode 7 is Maki Roll; it airs when daysPlayed = 49, i.e. Summer 21 Y1 (a Sunday), and again every two years (Summer 21 Y3...), plus possible Wednesday reruns. The Saloon (Gus) sells the recipe '(O)228 (Recipe)' for 300g with no condition.
Maki Roll recipe: 1 of any Fish (category -4) + 1 Seaweed (152) + 1 Rice (423); output 228. Pierre sells Rice. Needs a kitchen.
Fried Egg recipe: 1 of any Egg-category item (-5: Egg, Large Egg, Duck Egg, Void Egg, Golden Egg, Ostrich Egg); output 194; unlock 'default'. Needs a kitchen.
Fish Smoker (big craftable) costs 10 Hardwood (709) + 1 Sea Jelly + 1 River Jelly + 1 Cave Jelly.
Energy = ceil(Edibility x 2.5) + quality x Edibility for normal items, with two overrides: Stardrop (434) restores 999 energy and Life Elixir (773) restores 0 energy.
rules.fix: Special-case 434 -> 999 (full) and 773 -> 0 in energy().

rules.summary: Health = (int)(energy x 0.45) in single-precision (no difference from Python's int(e*0.45) for any vanilla value), except: edibility < 0 gives 0 health, Bug Steak 874 uses 0.68, Stardrop 434 and Energy Tonic 349 give 0, Life Elixir 773 gives 999.
rules.fix: Add 773 -> 999 and return 0 when edibility < 0.

rules.summary: Bug Steak (874) health = (int)(energy x 0.68).
Stardrop (434) and Energy Tonic (349) return 0 health. (Separately, Stardrop's energy is 999, not the formula.)

Sell price = (int)(price x (1 + 0.25 x quality)), then profession multipliers by category, then the farm's profit-margin setting (difficultyModifier) with a floor of 1. Cooked dishes (-7) have no profession bonus, but other edible items do (Tiller fruit/veg/flowers, Artisan -26, Rancher eggs/milk, Fisher/Angler fish, Tapper syrup).
rules.fix: Apply profession multipliers for non -7 foods and multiply by the profit-margin option (save <options> / difficultyModifier) if not 1.

rules.summary: Cooking needs a known recipe and a kitchen; kitchens are in the farmhouse/cabin from houseUpgradeLevel 1 and in the Ginger Island farmhouse. The cooking menu also draws ingredients from the kitchen fridge and mini-fridges.
rules.fix: Allow the island farmhouse; count fridge/mini-fridge contents as cooking inventory (the save parser currently misses the house fridge).

rules.summary: A negative ingredient id matches any item whose Category equals it (e.g. -4 any fish, -5 any egg, -6 any milk); quality is ignored. -777 is a special rule for any of the four seasonal wild-seed packs.
174 and 182 have identical edibility (15), price (95) and category (-5), so as food they are interchangeable.

Bush berries really are day-windowed (Spring 15-18, Fall 8-11). Location forage is chosen from Data/Locations Forage, filtered by Season and by Condition (e.g. Beach uses Condition 'LOCATION_SEASON Here spring summer fall' with no Season), then rolled against Chance; how many spawn per day is random.
rules.fix: Honour Forage Condition (at least LOCATION_SEASON), and show Chance rather than treating forage as guaranteed.

rules.summary: Base max stamina is 270; each Stardrop adds 34 (to 508), and MaxStamina buffs add on top. The save stores player <maxStamina>.
For non-negative energy, truncation to int equals floor, so floor(energy x 0.45) is the same as the game's cast (exceptions as in food.health-formula).

The game lets you eat any object whose Edibility is not -300. Edibility 0 (Daffodil, Sweet Pea, Crocus) and negative values (Sap -1, Holly, Red Mushroom, Pufferfish, Sea Cucumber, Void Egg/Mayonnaise, Goby...) are edible and drain energy. No Arch item has Edibility > 0, so the Arch exclusion does nothing.
rules.fix: Fine as 'food that restores energy'; say so, and drop the Arch clause (or keep for safety).

rules.summary: Buffs come from Data/Objects Buffs: Duration is in in-game minutes (-2 = rest of day; omitted with BuffId = Data/Buffs duration); CustomAttributes give the stats. Some foods only reference a BuffId with no CustomAttributes: Beer, Pale Ale, Wine, Mead (17 Tipsy), Oil of Garlic (23), Squid Ink Ravioli (28). Any non-normal quality multiplies the Data/Objects buff duration by 1.5, and cooked dishes (-7) of non-normal quality get +1 on each non-zero stat (farming, fishing, mining, luck, foraging, max energy, magnetism, defense, attack).
rules.fix: Keep BuffId-only buffs (look them up in Data/Buffs), apply the 1.5x duration for quality > 0 and the +1 stat bonus for quality cooked dishes.

rules.summary: Each spring day the Forest spawns Spring Onion forage crops in up to 7 random patches in its south-east area (x >= 70, y >= 68 region) on diggable tiles.

Medium bushes are in bloom Spring 15-18 (by the bush location's season); each such bush rolls about 20-26% per day to fruit, and shaking a fruiting non-town bush drops Salmonberry (296), 1 + ForagingLevel/4 of them.
Same mechanism, Fall 8-11, dropping Blackberry (410).

Winter Root (412) and Snow Yam (416) come from hoeing ordinary diggable ground in winter: 8% per freshly hoed tile, outdoors, off the Farm, not the Desert, not from bombs. Artifact spots don't give them (no Data/Locations ArtifactSpots entry does). Winter Seeds also grow them.
rules.fix: Describe as 'hoe bare ground off the farm in winter (8% per tile)'; not artifact spots, not the farm.

rules.summary: Cave Carrot (78) comes from Mines barrels/crates, hoeing Mines dirt, and as the fallback of the special mine-level item roll - any season.

In the Mines, the floor-object roll gives Red Mushroom (420) on levels > 20 except the 40-79 frost area: floors 21-39, 80-119 and the Skull Cavern. Mushroom floors (81-119, not multiples of 5) also scatter Red/Purple. On hard Mines difficulty, floors 40-69 can also have them.
rules.fix: Add Skull Cavern; note the dangerous-mines exception.

rules.summary: Purple Mushroom (422) needs level > 80: floors 81-119 and the Skull Cavern (mushroom floors raise the odds). Floor 80 itself does not qualify.
rules.fix: Say 81+ including Skull Cavern.

rules.summary: Forage comes from Data/Locations[loc].Forage (plus the 'Default' entry, empty in vanilla). Season absent means no season filter, but entries can carry a Condition (Beach shell entries use 'LOCATION_SEASON Here spring summer fall') and a per-spawn Chance.
rules.fix: Parse Condition (LOCATION_SEASON at least) and carry Chance.

rules.summary: Cooking field 3 values in data: 'f NPC N' (36): at N hearts the game mails '<NPC>Cooking' next day and reading it teaches the lowest-heart unknown 'f' recipe for that NPC; 's Skill N' (9) or a bare skill name + level: learned on reaching the level (unbuffed); 'default' (1): granted on load; 'l N' (34): informational only (TV/shop recipes, the game ignores it); 'null' (Cookies, from Evelyn's event).
rules.fix: Accept bare skill names ('Farming 3') as well as 's Farming 3'; label 'l' and 'null' explicitly instead of '(other)'.

rules.summary: Cooking recipe = 'ingredient pairs / unused / output id [count] (may list several outputs) / unlock / optional display name'; a negative ingredient id is a category; -777 = any wild-seed pack.

Crafting recipe = 'ingredients / location / output / bigCraftable bool / unlock / display name'; field 3 parsed as bool ('Ring' entries read as false). Crafted foods are Field Snack (s Foraging 1), Oil of Garlic (s Combat 6), Life Elixir (s Combat 2), Bug Steak (s Combat 1).
Fried Egg: 1 any Egg (-5), recipe 'default'. The first house upgrade costs 10,000g AND 450 Wood and takes 3 days.
rules.fix: Add 450 Wood and 3 days to the kitchen cost; 'any egg', not just Egg.

rules.summary: Maki Roll: any Fish + Seaweed + Rice (Pierre). Recipe: Queen of Sauce Summer 21 Y1 (and Y3...), or Gus's Saloon for 300g any time. Kitchen = 10,000g + 450 Wood.
rules.fix: Mention the Saloon recipe (300g) and the 450 Wood.

rules.summary: Fried Egg's unlock field is 'default', so every player is granted it (added on load if missing); needs 1 egg (any -5).
Same formulas as food.py, inheriting its gaps: Stardrop energy 999, Life Elixir energy 0 / health 999, negative edibility -> 0 health.
rules.fix: Fix in food.energy/health; answers.py follows.

rules.summary: The calendar lists a villager's birthday (Data/Characters BirthSeason/BirthDay) only if they exist (UnlockConditions: Kent from Year 2, Leo once he's moved to the valley) and their Calendar setting allows it: HiddenAlways never, HiddenUntilMet once you've met them (the Dwarf, Sandy, Krobus).

The bookseller visits on two days a season: candidate days Spring 11,12,21,22,25 / Summer 9,12,18,25,27 / Fall 4,7,8,9,12,19,22,25 / Winter 5,11,12,19,22,24; one is picked with Next(count) from a generator seeded (year×11, game id, season index), the other is half the list further on (wrapping).
Green rain falls on one summer day every year, picked from 5, 6, 7, 14, 15, 16, 18, 23 with a generator seeded (year×777, game id); the weather data puts GreenRain first (IS_GREEN_RAIN_DAY).

Shop door hours are tile actions on the outdoor maps ('LockedDoorWarp <x> <y> <building> <open> <close> [<villager> <friendship points>]'): you can enter from <open> until before <close>. A friendship door (Leah, Elliott, Maru's room: 500 points) ignores the friendship rule in winter. The town key opens valley doors at any hour (not Night Market ones other than the Fish Shop), and in Year 1 green rain leaves doors unlocked except on the Beach and Forest maps and the Adventurer's Guild.
data: Maps/Town, Mountain, Forest, Beach, Desert tile property Action LockedDoorWarp

rules.summary: Most shops need their keeper in place: Pierre on tile (4,17); Gus anywhere in x 9-18, y 17-18 of the Saloon; Robin within 3 tiles of (8,19); Marnie on (11-13,14) unless the Animal Catalogue has been read; Willy at y <= 5 in the Fish Shop; any villager at the clinic desk (x 4-7, y 15); Clint anywhere in the Blacksmith; Sandy anywhere in the Oasis. Marlon's shop and JojaMart need no one. Where keepers stand comes from their schedules.
data: Maps/SeedShop, Saloon, ScienceHouse, AnimalShop, Blacksmith, FishShop, Hospital shop tile actions

rules.summary: Each animal's night is rolled with a generator seeded (animal id / 2, days played of the new day), so tomorrow's produce follows from tonight's state: petting (+15 friendship, + max(5, 30 + drain) happiness, doubled with the coop/barn profession), not petting (friendship - (10 - F/200), happiness - 50), door shut (+2 x drain), hay if fullness < 200, growing a day if full, hunger (-100 happiness, -20 friendship), then the produce gate (days since last >= DaysToProduce minus the faster-produce friendship/profession, rolls under fullness/200 and happiness/70, not a baby). Quality is rerolled only in the happiness/150 branch (q = F/1000 - (1 - H/225), +0.33 with the quality profession; iridium needs q >= 0.95); otherwise the last quality carries over.

Help Wanted item requests pick from: gems/minerals/fishing finds (68 66 78 80 86 152 167 153 420), more gems past mine floor 40 (62 70 72 84 422) and 80 (64 60 82) or once the bottom is reached, desert finds with ccVault (88 90 164 165), bars with the Furnace recipe (334 335 336 338) and Refined Quartz with the Quartz Globe, the season's forage and fish, the season's crops possible now (only the early ones in the first week; some Year 2+ or with the Vault; none in winter), and known dishes whose ingredients all come from that pool. Egg and Milk categories become a plain Egg or Milk.

Every night the Beach scatters items on the tide pools (tiles 65-89 x 11-22, east of the broken bridge): a run of rolls that keeps going while a roll falls under a shrinking chance, each item a Sea Urchin 1 time in 5, else Coral. They're only reachable once the bridge is repaired (Beach bridgeFixed, 300 Wood).
In winter, hoeing soil outdoors off the farm (not in the Desert) has an 8% chance a tile to turn up a Winter Root or a Snow Yam (half each), twice with a Generous hoe at 50%.

A shop entry with IsRecipe sells the recipe for the item, not the item: the Saloon's (O)228 at 300g is the Maki Roll recipe. The Saloon's only cooked dish for sale is DISH_OF_THE_DAY, the save's dishOfTheDay (chosen when the day starts), sold at its standard sale price (price x 2) with the stack as the stock.

Lewis scores the Fair's grange display as 14, plus per item quality + 1 (iridium +5) and a point for each sale-price mark it reaches (20, 90, 200; 300 below gold; 400 at normal quality; the item's real sale price), plus 5 per different kind up to 30 (vegetables, fruit, animal goods, gems and minerals, fish, forage/flowers/syrups, cooking, artisan goods), plus 9 - 2 per empty slot (nine slots). 90+ wins 1,000 star tokens, 75+ 500, 60+ 250, else 50; Lewis's shorts on display skip judging for 750. Any small object can go on it, one per slot.

Harvesting a crop gives farming XP once per harvest, however many items drop: round(16·ln(0.018·price + 1)) with the harvest's base price. Levels need 100, 380, 770, 1300, 2150, 3300, 4800, 6900, 10000 and 15000 XP in all.

In Year 1 Clint sells Copper Ore 75g, Iron Ore 150g, Coal 150g and Gold Ore 400g; from Year 2, 150 / 250 / 250 / 750g. A bar is 5 ore and 1 coal in a Furnace, so in Year 1 a Gold Bar can be bought for about 2,150g.
The Seed Maker recipe is learned at Farming 9 and takes 25 Wood, 10 Coal and 1 Gold Bar.
